facts.statement: The genus Asteriornis was described by Field and colleagues in 2020.
Asteriornis lived during the Late Maastrichtian stage of the Cretaceous period.
The fossil remains of Asteriornis were found at the CBR-Romontbos quarry near Eben-Emael in Belgium.
facts.quote: It was retrieved from four blocks of sediment found at the CBR-Romontbos quarry near Eben-Emael in the Maastricht Formation of Belgium

facts.statement: Asteriornis lived approximately 66.8 to 66.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: It is dated to around 66.8 to 66.7 million years old

facts.statement: Asteriornis was a small, long-legged bird that inhabited coastal environments.
facts.quote: It was a small, long-legged bird that lived near the coastline

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Asteriornis is estimated to have weighed around 394 grams.
facts.quote: The holotype of Asteriornis is estimated around 394 g

facts.statement: Asteriornis possessed a slightly downcurved and lightweight beak.
facts.quote: The beak was slightly downcurved and lightweight

facts.statement: The leg bones of Asteriornis were elongated and slender, resembling those of modern ground-dwelling birds.
facts.quote: Leg bones are elongated and slender, similar in proportions and structure to modern ground-living birds

facts.statement: Researchers infer that Asteriornis had a terrestrial lifestyle and a generalist diet, which may have helped it survive the extinction event.
facts.quote: Small size, a terrestrial lifestyle, and a generalist diet have all been inferred as ecological advantages possessed by early neornithes

facts.statement: Asteriornis is considered one of the oldest known birds definitively belonging to the group Neornithes (modern birds).
facts.quote: Asteriornis is one of the oldest-known birds irrefutably belonging to the group Neornithes

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Asteriornis near the base of the superorder Galloanserae, which includes chickens and ducks.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis placed Asteriornis near the base of Galloanserae

facts.statement: Some studies suggest Asteriornis might be a paleognath related to tinamous and lithornithids, though this classification has limited support.
facts.quote: At least two studies in 2021 and 2024 recovered Asteriornis as a paleognath, sister to Lithornithidae and Tinamidae, albeit "with limited support"

facts.statement: Recent analyses in 2025 placed Asteriornis within Galloanserae as a stem-galliform, but researchers could not confirm a specific jaw feature previously thought to be present.
facts.quote: In June 2025, Crane and colleagues placed Asteriornis within the crown-group Galloanserae based on their phylogenetic analyses, specifically as a stem-galliform, though the authors were unable to find a galloanseran-like retroarticular process unlike previously assumed

facts.statement: The discoverers nicknamed Asteriornis the "Wonderchicken" due to its unique characteristics.
facts.quote: The researchers who discovered and described the fossil gave Asteriornis the nickname "Wonderchicken"

facts.statement: The radius bone of Asteriornis flattened and widened toward the wrist, featuring a large hooked bump.
facts.quote: The radius fragment flattens and widens towards the wrist, where it possesses a large hooked bump

facts.statement: The Maastricht Formation where Asteriornis was found is named after the final stage of the Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: This geological formation is the namesake of the Maastrichtian stage, which was the last stage of the Cretaceous period and the Mesozoic era

facts.statement: Asteriornis exhibits physical traits of both galliforms (chicken-like) and anseriforms (duck-like) birds.
facts.quote: It possesses characteristics of both galliformes (chicken-like birds) and anseriformes (duck-like birds)

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Asteriornis as 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The fossil was first discovered in 2000 by the amateur paleontologist Maarten van Dinther.
rejected.quote: It was first unearthed in 2000, by amateur paleontologist Maarten van Dinther
